quarterly_data.signal: Fiscal year ended March 2026 results: revenue JPY 2,070,203 million, up 2.8% from JPY 2,014,454 million; operating profit JPY 118,138 million, up 332.8% (margin 5.7% vs 1.4%); profit before tax JPY 168,994 million, up 165.6%; profit attributable to owners of the parent JPY 140,969 million, up 485.0%. Gross margin rose from 27.8% to 29.4%. Management states AI and data center demand stayed at a high level in its main semiconductor and information and communications markets; revenue rose as the Core Components segment, led by semiconductor-related components, grew, while the Solutions segment declined mainly on the January 2026 sale of US subsidiary Kyocera Industrial Tools, Inc. Profit rose on the gain on that sale, higher revenue and structural reform progress, against an impairment loss of JPY 40,148 million in the semiconductor components organic materials business in the prior year. No single external customer accounted for 10% or more of revenue.
quarterly_data.figure: Revenue JPY 2,070,203 million (+2.8%); operating profit JPY 118,138 million (+332.8%); net profit JPY 140,969 million (+485.0%)

quarterly_data.signal: Core Components segment, fiscal year ended March 2026: revenue JPY 653,429 million, up 10.4%; business profit JPY 63,082 million (margin 9.7%) vs a loss of JPY 1,889 million. Within it, Semiconductor-Related Components revenue JPY 379,432 million, up 16.0% from JPY 327,049 million, with profit of JPY 46,933 million (margin 12.4%) vs a loss of JPY 26,447 million; Industrial and Automotive Components revenue JPY 250,069 million, up 3.4%. Management states revenue grew mainly on higher sales of ceramic packages for the information and communications market and organic packages for data centers; profit rose on higher revenue, structural reform and lower one-time losses (this year about JPY 10.0 billion, mainly a write-down of idle assets in the semiconductor components organic materials business and an impairment in the former display business of the automotive systems business, vs about JPY 43.0 billion in the prior year, mainly impairment in the organic materials business). From January 1, 2026 part of the Industrial and Automotive Components business is managed within Semiconductor-Related Components.
quarterly_data.figure: Semiconductor-Related Components revenue JPY 379,432 million (+16.0%), profit JPY 46,933 million (12.4%); Core Components revenue JPY 653,429 million (+10.4%)

quarterly_data.signal: Orders received, fiscal year ended March 2026: total JPY 2,098,265 million, up 3.4%; Core Components JPY 640,923 million, up 9.1%, of which Semiconductor-Related Components JPY 361,435 million, up 15.6% from JPY 312,542 million; Electronic Components JPY 373,179 million, up 5.7%; Solutions JPY 1,100,790 million, down 0.8%. The company states its production tracks sales, so it reports production with the segment sales figures.
quarterly_data.figure: Orders JPY 2,098,265 million (+3.4%); Semiconductor-Related Components orders JPY 361,435 million (+15.6%)

quarterly_data.signal: Other segments, fiscal year ended March 2026: Electronic Components revenue JPY 363,486 million, up 2.5%, business profit JPY 7,316 million (margin 2.0%) — management states higher sales of capacitors for the automotive and information and communications markets at the Kyocera AVX Components group outweighed the strong yen, and profit included a one-time loss of about JPY 1.50 billion on the transfer of the silicon diode / power semiconductor business. Solutions revenue JPY 1,070,919 million, down 1.4%, business profit JPY 103,943 million (margin 9.7% vs 6.8%), including a one-time gain of about JPY 17.0 billion on the sale of Kyocera Industrial Tools, Inc.
quarterly_data.figure: Electronic Components revenue JPY 363,486 million (+2.5%); Solutions revenue JPY 1,070,919 million (-1.4%)

quarterly_data.signal: Capex was JPY 149,099 million in the fiscal year ended March 2026, up 5.0%, mainly to expand production capacity to meet rising demand for products for the semiconductor-related and information and communications markets; Core Components capex was JPY 78,759 million, up 64.3% from JPY 47,923 million. Plan for the fiscal year ending March 2027: capex of JPY 225,000 million, up 50.9%, to further expand production mainly for semiconductor-related and information and communications market products (equipment for capacity increases and productivity improvement in every segment), and R&D expense of JPY 120,000 million. Equipment purchase commitments totalled JPY 100,452 million at fiscal year end, of which JPY 96,925 million falls due in the year ending March 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 capex JPY 149,099 million (Core Components JPY 78,759 million, +64.3%); FY2027 plan capex JPY 225,000 million (+50.9%), R&D JPY 120,000 million

quarterly_data.signal: R&D: expense JPY 115,701 million (5.6% of revenue) in the fiscal year ended March 2026, of which Core Components JPY 26,120 million, up 22.0%. In semiconductor-related components the company states AI data centers and network equipment push for higher speed, larger capacity and lower power, with rising demand for optical transmission; its ceramic materials business is developing packages for high-speed optical communication, opto-electronic integrated modules, ultra-small thin high-strength packages for electronic devices and sensors, and ceramic core substrates for chiplet packages, and its organic materials business is focused on high-end large-size, high-layer-count packages. For semiconductor manufacturing equipment it is developing parts and materials for next-generation tools for advanced semiconductors (fine wiring, 3D structures) and new high-thermal-conductivity materials.
quarterly_data.figure: R&D JPY 115,701 million (Core Components JPY 26,120 million, +22.0%)

quarterly_data.signal: Company targets and strategy: ROE of 5.0% or more in the fiscal year ending March 2028, 8.0% or more in the fiscal year ending March 2031, and 10.0% or more in the future; ROIC is introduced as a business evaluation metric from the next fiscal year. Management positions the components businesses (Core Components and Electronic Components) as the medium- to long-term growth driver, concentrating resources on focus areas such as the semiconductor-related market and targeting share gains and higher profitability mainly in advanced semiconductors and mobility, while Solutions is to generate steady profit. Management states the AI market is expected to expand into new applications such as robotics and social infrastructure, requiring higher-performance, lower-power semiconductors.
quarterly_data.figure: ROE target 5.0%+ (FY ending March 2028), 8.0%+ (FY ending March 2031), 10.0%+ longer term

quarterly_data.signal: On January 22, 2026 the board resolved to transfer all shares of a company to be newly established to Sumitomo Bakelite and signed the share transfer agreement the same day; the transfer is scheduled for the end of October 2026. Before closing, Kyocera will move into the new company, by absorption-type split, its chemical business run within the semiconductor components ceramic materials division, which makes and sells semiconductor-related products centred on encapsulants and pastes, plus chemical and composite products.

To grow its connector business, Kyocera signed a capital and business alliance agreement with Japan Aviation Electronics Industry and acquired shares in it for cash during the fiscal year ended March 2026 (accounted for by the equity method).

Main package plants at March 31, 2026: organic substrate production equipment at the Kyoto Ayabe Plant and the Kagoshima Sendai Plant (which also makes ceramic packages and fine ceramic parts); ceramic packages also at the Shiga Higashiomi Plant, the Kagoshima Kokubu Plant, Kyocera Vietnam (Hung Yen) and Kyocera International (San Diego). On April 1, 2026 the Kagoshima Kokubu and Kagoshima Hayato plants were merged and renamed the Kagoshima Kirishima Plant.
